title: A to-do list
description:
Write an interactive to-do list. It reads commands after the prompt `> ` until `quit`:

| Command | Does | Prints |
|---|---|---|
| `add <text>` | Adds a task (the rest of the line, spaces kept) | `Added #<n>: <text>` |
| `list` | Shows every task, numbered from 1 | `<n>. [ ] <text>` or `<n>. [x] <text>`; `Nothing to do.` if there are none |
| `done <n>` | Marks task n as done | `Done: <text>` |
| `undo <n>` | Marks task n as not done | `Undone: <text>` |
| `remove <n>` | Deletes task n (later tasks move up) | `Removed: <text>` |
| `clear` | Deletes every finished task | `Cleared <k> task(s).` |
| `quit` | Ends | `Bye! <k> of <n> done.` |

- An empty line does nothing. Commands are not case-sensitive (`ADD`, `List`), but the task text keeps its case.
- `add` without text prints `Nothing to add.`
- For `done`, `undo` and `remove`: if `n` is not a whole number, print `Not a number: <n>`; if there is no such task, print `No task <n>`; without `n`, print `Which task?`.
- Anything else prints `Unknown command: <word>`.

```
> add buy milk
Added #1: buy milk
> add Call Ada
Added #2: Call Ada
> done 1
Done: buy milk
> list
1. [x] buy milk
2. [ ] Call Ada
> quit
Bye! 1 of 2 done.
```
hints: `line.split(maxsplit=1)` splits off the first word and keeps the rest of the line, spaces included, as the second item.
Store each task as a small list `[text, done]` so marking it done can change it in place.
requirements: Every command and every error message works as described.
Task numbers always follow the current list order.
stretch: Save the list to a file when quitting and load it at start (lesson 3.05), and add `edit <n> <text>` and priorities.

examples.name: the example
examples.stdin:
add buy milk
add Call Ada
done 1
list
quit
examples.expected:
> Added #1: buy milk
> Added #2: Call Ada
> Done: buy milk
> 1. [x] buy milk
2. [ ] Call Ada
> Bye! 1 of 2 done.

examples.name: removing and numbering
examples.stdin:
add one
add two
add three
remove 2
list
done 2
list
quit
examples.expected:
> Added #1: one
> Added #2: two
> Added #3: three
> Removed: two
> 1. [ ] one
2. [ ] three
> Done: three
> 1. [ ] one
2. [x] three
> Bye! 1 of 2 done.

add c
done 1
done 3
clear
list

> Added #2: b

> Done: a

> 1. [ ] b

> 1. [ ] b

tests.name: errors
tests.stdin:
list
done
done x
done 4
add
fly away

ADD Shout
List
quit
tests.expected:
> Nothing to do.
> Which task?
> Not a number: x
> No task 4
> Nothing to add.
> Unknown command: fly
> > Added #1: Shout
> 1. [ ] Shout
> Bye! 0 of 1 done.
